thread.title: How Twitter Predicted The Disappointment From Apple

author: Andy Swan
title: How Twitter Predicted The Disappointment From Apple
text:
After the Apple Keynote event in September, we told you that Apple would be facing an uphill battle in 2019 . Enthusiasm for their new iPhone lineup was lackluster, by Apple standards. Yesterday, we got confirmation that our prediction was correct, as Apple announced that holiday iPhone sales were likely to disappoint investors .
To come to this kind of prediction, we at LikeFolio constantly monitor consumer conversations on Twitter for indications of how much, and how enthusiastically, people talking about purchasing new products.
Historically, the consumer reaction to the annual Keynote event has been an incredible predictor of $AAPL stock , having predicted the movement of AAPL stock over the following 9 months for five straight years. Here is what we were seeing in the aftermath of the September keynote announcement of the iPhone XS:
Consumer response to Apple's new product lineup was the lowest we have seen in years. LikeFolio
As you can see from the chart above, purchase intent mentions of Apple products in the two days surrounding the keynote event were much lower in 2018 than they had been in prior years. That told us that consumers simply weren't enthusiastic about the phones compared to their level of excitement in prior years.
Lead time is your friend
When assessing the impact of a shift in purchase intent mentions, it's important that we understand how consumers typically go about buying that product.
For example, when analyzing purchase intent mentions of burritos from Chipotle, we would expect that people were talking about a purchase that they made very recently or were about to make fairly soon.
With iPhones, the lead time is significantly longer than most items for several key reasons:
iPhones cost $1000. That kind of expense usually takes people a longer time to execute. Phone sales are often dependent upon the consumer's upgrade cycle with their provider. Tweeting that you are going to get the iPhone XS is likely to mean that you'll do so when your current contract expires. iPhones are often given as Christmas gifts. This creates a natural lead time that means the purchase intent mention during the keynote in September is actually more likely to be revenue in Apple's pocket in the 4th quarter. This extended lead time is a big part of the reason that we've seen reaction to Apple's keynote event as a successful indicator of Apple's success (or struggles) over the following 9 month time frame. That's a much longer lead time than we typically see for consumer-facing companies. It simply takes that long for consumers' enthusiasm during product announcements to translate into reported revenue for the company.
What's next for Apple?
Getting confirmation that our hypothesis is on track gives us confidence in the analysis of the data moving forward, and especially as we dive into the brand level.
So here are three more Apple predictions that we're comfortable making based on consumer purchase intent mentions captured from Twitter:
The Apple Watch will continue to gain significant traction.
The Apple Watch Series 4 was the runaway hit of the 2018 Apple Keynote LikeFolio
Apple will downplay the importance of iPhone advancements going forward. They've already started doing this, focusing the company's efforts on new devices and services while ending the reporting of iPhone unit sales. AAPL stock will continue to struggle well into the first half of 2019. Whatever happens with Apple from here, we can rest assured that it will be consumers on Main Street, not analysts on Wall Street, that clue us in first.
